nodes.label: The 'no forced rehandshake on endpoint change' premise was already obsolete
nodes.rationale: set_peer_endpoint -> apply_peer_endpoint_scoped -> uapi::set_one_peer is literally remove-then-add, so the re-created peer starts with no noise session and the caller must nudge boringtun. The forced-rehandshake mechanism already exists and is the default; CLAUDE.md's 'rekey-free endpoint switch' wording was corrected in PR #43.

nodes.label: The cutover seam is guarded in three places, not one
nodes.rationale: punch_and_apply's loop-head guard, set_peer_endpoint's atomic-commit guard, and run_path_ticks's corroboration gate all refuse a Relayed peer — the last of which suppresses the cutover's own success signal via the very flag the probe must clear.

nodes.label: There is no cutover rollback anywhere today
nodes.rationale: punch_and_apply on Exhausted logs and returns, leaving WG on the last dead candidate; a rollback must also restore the live_endpoints pin to the relay socket or the next apply_state resurrects the direct endpoint, and it costs a SECOND session reset of the relay leg — not in the <=6s budget.

nodes.label: Rotation hard-skip — Role-A overlap is not observable from PathCtx
Relayed→Direct is not a settled-boundary crossing, so it produces no prompt report
nodes.rationale: Round 4 deliberately excluded within-settled moves to avoid report chatter; the one edge a controller-driven cutover sweep most needs is the one that optimisation removed — decisive for driving the cutover gateway-local instead.

nodes.label: Owner decision: drive the cutover gateway-local, drop CutoverProbe
nodes.rationale: The gateway already holds the peer's candidates in DesiredState; the controller only adds go-time synchronisation, which matters far less for a cutover into an already-open port-restricted mapping than for a cold punch. Also removes the need for a second sweep timer, which MAX_PERIODIC_ATTEMPTS/RETRY_INTERVAL could not express anyway.

nodes.label: Broker::on_report stale-snapshot race — re-graded to an availability bug
nodes.rationale: The comment's own bounding argument — that the gateway's directive-independent StartPunch recovery limits impact — was falsified by the authoritative case-4 run: unsynchronized self-timers can never land a port-restricted pair. Scope correction: the generation must gate the whole Report handler, since set_applied_version and set_local_candidates run off the same stale request.

nodes.label: First-boot IR schema mismatch is now a silent blackhole, not a crash
nodes.rationale: PR #43 moved the decode into the worker's non-fatal path, so a gateway booting against a too-new controller with no prior good policy attaches its default-deny enforcer and drops all fabric traffic while looking healthy to systemd/Kubernetes. That raises the value of X-6's Watch-open and enroll-time gates — they become the only things preventing it, where the crash was at least loud.

nodes.label: GAP — the operator turns an enroll version rejection into a silent hang
Case 2 (relayed→direct) collides with relay_matrix case 4's phase-2 assertion
nodes.rationale: Case 4 panics if either side leaves relayed during a 5s settle after unblock_direct, and stays green only by the 20s PROBE_DIRECT_INTERVAL grace — a timing coincidence, not a basis, so it must be reconciled deliberately as a modification rather than a pure addition.
